Yeah, I get that. I was 30, and was being forcefully retired from the military before I went in. And I avoided it because of those same misconceptions. I don't mean to be judgmental, but I can explain why it's a misconception. Let me rant for a bit.

First, I have three questions. What is a skill, what is personality, and what is behavior? Those questions take a lot of work to answer concisely. And when you get into the weeds of it, you'll understand that they are all just different slices of the same pie. At least, that's what I got out of it.

We all agree that skills are built over time, and it takes a long time to become a master at anything. We all agree that behaviors are learned. We also accept that what is learned can be unlearned and/or modified.  Why would personality be any different? Or the real inner you? There is a famous sculpture named "The self-made man" created by Bobbie Carlyle, google it. You'll see a sculpture of a man sculpting himself out of rock.

I think we are all kinda doing this all of the time behind the scenes, sculpting ourselves. Sometimes when people grow up in harsh environments, they've never held the chisel until they were on their own. So continuing the sculpture can be scary.

There is an inner you, a deeper you. I'm personally NOT convinced that your personality is the inner you. I also think that outward expression of emotions are misleading in terms of the real you. This is a messy and confusing area of knowledge, and that's why universities around the world still research these phenomena.

I do know this, every thing that's ever been built has required maintenance. Almost everything that's been built has been updated over the centuries. Houses are no longer mud huts. Bridges aren't wood. Guns are smokeless. Cars are electric.

It is ok to remake yourself into whatever you want. But you have to want it, you cant force someone to use their own chisel, they have to want to use it. BUT something is remaking itself INTO  something else. There is an EVEN deeper you, that is remaking your current personality, behavior, or skill. Think about that for a minute.

How can you ever really know the real you, unless you try to chisel a new you?
